# `proj path get`

Get the resolved absolute path for a given label in the project.

```bash
proj path get --label <LABEL> [--target final|safe] [--format auto|absolute|relative] [--relative-to BASE] [--project <PATH>] [PART ...]
```

## Declared directory paths

A label must be declared in the active configuration with a nonempty `path`.
ASCII case is ignored. Undeclared labels and suffixes are errors: declaring
`raw-data` does not declare `raw` or `raw-data-extra`. Relative paths resolve
against the captured project root; explicit external directories are allowed.
Queries do not create directories. Final lookup returns the configured location;
explicit safe lookup resolves the logical versioned-cache target.

## Explicit and inherited project root

`--project PATH` selects that exact existing directory, including a folder
without configuration or VERSION. It overrides both ancestor discovery and an
inherited run root. Invalid directories fail with a nonzero exit status.

The CLI captures an absolute root as `PROJ_PROJECT_ROOT` for the invocation and
its child processes. A nested `proj path get` uses that root even after a script
changes cwd. An invalid inherited root fails rather than falling back silently.
Direct Rust `build_project(root, ...)` calls also pass their supplied root to
children. See the discovery rules below for the recognized root markers.

This establishes CLI child-query behavior, not direct Quarto/RStudio parity or
changes to the existing R frontend. Renderer configuration, execution cwd,
resource links and output placement remain separate concerns. Path queries do
not write ignore files or create the resolved target directories.

## Nearest-root discovery

Without `--project` or an inherited run root, discovery walks upward from cwd and
selects the first recognized directory. It does not search downward for projects.
Recognized markers are VERSION, README.md, `_quarto.yml`, `_proj.yml`, legacy
`_projr.yml`, Git/SVN metadata, a DESCRIPTION containing `Package: `, an RStudio
`.Rproj` whose first line starts `Version: `, and a renv.lock with a Packages map.

`pyproject.toml`, `Project.toml` and `JuliaProject.toml` deliberately extend the
projr marker set for Python/Julia. `requirements.txt` and `Manifest.toml` alone
are not root markers. Standalone VERSION and README markers are retained, so a
nested directory with one is the nearer project; explicit selection overrides it.

Marker recognition does not change shallow default script enumeration or prove
that the corresponding language runner/frontend is implemented. Legacy config
content handling is a separate compatibility change from recognizing its root.

If no recognized marker exists, discovery selects cwd. Discovery success does not
mean a build is configured: the current product contract requires active root
configuration and explicit used-directory mappings. Validation changes enforcing
that newer contract are separate from this root-discovery slice.


## Explicit safe lookup and file fragments

`--target safe` maps declared output/data/docs-class labels to
`<selected-cache>/projr/v<active-version>/<exact-declared-label>`.
One explicit `safe: true` cache wins; otherwise eligible exact label `cache` wins,
then the first eligible cache in merged declaration order. `safe: false` excludes
a candidate. The chosen label is captured for child queries. A release version has no dev suffix; dev cache
keys use a hyphen, such as `v1.2.3-4`. Other roles retain their configured targets.

`--target final` addresses the explicitly configured destination, including an
absolute external directory. This intermediate slice retains `final` as the CLI
default until build promotion is wired to safe logical output; that is a temporary
compatibility boundary, not the final approved default path model.

Optional parts extend the selected role, for example:

```bash
proj path get --label output --target safe figures result.png
```

Queries do not create directories. Unknown labels, missing cache/version for safe
lookup, absolute/drive-qualified parts and parent traversal fail clearly. Explicit
directory mappings stay mandatory; `output-model` does not imply an `output` alias.
Native cwd/auto-relative presentation and renderer staging are separate slices.


## Representation and explicit renderer context

`--format auto` returns a caller-cwd-relative filesystem path in ordinary execution
and an absolute target in an explicitly known managed render child. It never infers
render context from a .qmd filename, project marker or cwd. `absolute` and `relative`
override auto. Explicit `--relative-to cwd|project|document|/absolute/base` requires
relative format; document requires an individually known render document. Project
renders without a single document reject that base. A custom base must be absolute.

Strict relative conversion fails across roots/drives. Auto ordinary execution falls
back to absolute when no relative path exists; the absolute target stays identical.
The intermediate CLI still defaults to absolute/final until integrated consumers
switch to the approved auto/safe defaults. Getters create no directories.

Renderer descriptors are private per-command snapshots created only when launching
Quarto/rmarkdown/Bookdown, alongside unchanged root/profile/version/mapping inputs.
Ordinary scripts and dependency probes keep ordinary context. Existing R helpers
do not consume this descriptor; direct IDE rendering does not gain automatic parity.
Absolute results are filesystem targets, not literal Markdown/LaTeX URL rewrites.
